title: Mate in two: a quiet move
line: The first move threatens; every answer allows mate.

steps.text: Both of your checks here fail: the king or rook just takes the queen. The winning first move is not a check at all.
Take the pawn on f7 with the rook. It is not check, but it guards h7 and threatens mate there.

wrong.h6h7: The king takes the queen. Nothing guards h7 yet.
wrong.h6g7: The rook or the king takes the queen.

steps.hint: The rook goes up the open file and takes.
steps.after: Black has a move, but no move stops the queen from taking on h7.

steps.hint: Your rook and queen both reach the square next to the king, and each guards the other.
steps.after: Checkmate. A quiet move set it up, and nothing could stop it.

steps.text: Now you are Black. Your queen would mate on g2 if one more piece guarded it. Bring a piece to guard it, quietly.

wrong.g4g2: The king takes the queen. Nothing guards g2 yet.
wrong.g4g1: The rook or the king takes the queen.

steps.hint: Your knight can jump to a square that guards g2.
steps.after: The knight guards g2. White has no move that stops the queen from going there.

steps.hint: The queen goes to the square the knight guards.

summary: When no check works, look for a quiet move that threatens mate. If no answer stops it, it is mate in two.
